{{short description|Polish philosopher}}
[[File:Henryk Struve portret by Maleszewski.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Henryk Struve, portrait by {{ill|Tytus Maleszewski|pl}}, 1876]]
'''Henryk Struve''' (also known as '''Florian Gąsiorowski''') (1840–1912) was a Polish philosopher. He has been called "perhaps the most remarkable person in logic in [[Warsaw]] in the 19th century".<ref>{{cite book|author=Jan Woleński|authorlink=Jan Woleński|editor1=Andrzej Ehrenfeucht |editor2=V. Wiktor Marek |editor3=Marian Srebrny |title=Andrzej Mostowski and Foundational Studies| chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Ri4kjs-iGRgC&pg=PA30|access-date=25 November 2012|year=2008|publisher=IOS Press|isbn=978-1-58603-782-6|page=30|chapter=Mathematical Logic in Warsaw: 1918-1939}}</ref> Struve taught philosophy at [[Warsaw University]] from 1862 to 1903.<ref>{{cite book|editor=Anders Ahlqvist|title=Diversions of Galway: Papers on the History of Linguistics from ICHoLS V, Galway, Ireland, 1-6 September 1990|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=o2DW5p9yWbYC&pg=PA320|access-date=25 November 2012|year=1992|publisher=John Benjamins Publishing| isbn=978-90-272-4555-7|page=320}}</ref> He wrote works in Polish, German and Russian.{{citation needed|date=March 2017}}
